newsitem.title: USA: U.S. electricity demand growth to slow in 1997-EIA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. electricity demand growth to slow in 1997-EIA.

text.p: U.S. demand growth for electricity in 1997 is expected to slow to 0.8 percent, down from 1996's 2.8 percent growth rate, on expectations for a return to more moderate winter temperatures, the Energy Information Administration said Friday.
In its short-term outlook, the EIA projected electricity demand in 1997 at 3,282.4 billion kilowatthours, up from 3,254.8 billion in 1996.
It projected 1998 demand at 3,326.6 billion kilowatthours, up 1.3 percent from 1997's estimate.
Prices per kilowatthour were seen slipping to 8.29 cents in 1997 from 1996's 8.37 cents, and down to 8.21 cents in 1998, the EIA said.
Residential demand was projected to rise in 1997 to 1,100.5 billion kilowatthours from 1996's 1,087.3 billion, and to go to 1,127.2 billion in 1998.
Industrial demand was seen rising from 1,017.7 billion kilowatthours in 1996 to 1,022.7 billion in 1997 and to 1,027.8 billion in 1998.
